question: Can a stablecoin's issuer change while the coin, wallet and checkout stay the same?
answer: Yes. Tether moved all of USD₮'s obligations to a new company effective January 27, 2025 without users changing wallets, and SoFi's current SOFID terms already allow a substitute issuer. PayPal moved its wallet customers to PayPal Digital on May 19, 2026, but Paxos stayed PYUSD's issuer. Circle's planned move to a New York issuer, Ripple's reserve bank and Fiserv's FIUSD programs are still plans. In each case the ticker, app and checkout can stay the same while the legal party behind them changes, so the proof is a signed transfer and new terms, not the app.

sections.title: Change of issuer
sections.sub: The six change-of-issuer cards of the GENIUS Act control-plane deck, as of July 28, 2026, with newer charter records where the library has them.

items.title: Circle plans separate companies for today's issuer, the future issuer and the reserve bank
kv: plan stated by Circle · not in effect
Circle group, plus the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
Who issues USDC, and who manages and holds its reserves
A New York limited-purpose trust is set up and approved, and issuance actually moves to it
Circle Internet Financial, LLC is the current issuer. Circle stated a plan for a separate New York trust to issue. Circle National Trust is a reserve and custody bank that does not issue.
Possibly the same USDC and Circle Mint service, under new legal terms.
Existing integrations can keep working if contract addresses and support stay the same.
NYDFS charter or approval, exact legal name, permitted payment stablecoin issuer (PPSI) status, novation or new terms, and matching attestations.
Naming Circle National Trust as issuer, or treating the planned New York entity as already operating.
The plan appears in Circle's OCC application record. It is not evidence that the issuer change has closed.
Newer record (Fed accounts and charters master)
Circle (Circle National Trust): charter status 'opened'; latest step September 30, 2026: Listed on the OCC's active trust banks list.

items.title: Ripple's proposed national bank would manage RLUSD reserves, not issue the coin
kv: Standard Custody, Ripple National Trust Bank and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
RLUSD reserve management, collateral trustee role and custody
The charter is finalized and operations move over
Standard Custody remains the RLUSD issuer. The proposed national trust said it did not currently plan to issue stablecoins.
No required change to the RLUSD claim or wallet.
Final OCC approval and start of operations, reserve agreements in force and current RLUSD terms.
Treating the proposed bank as the new issuer.
Preliminary conditional approval does not mean the bank is operating.
Newer record (Fed accounts and charters master)
Ripple: charter status 'conditional approval'; latest step September 30, 2026: Not on the OCC's active trust banks list (not yet open).

items.title: FIUSD looks like a service built on Paxos and Circle, with no single named issuer
kv: watching marketing and launch date · issuer not identified
Fiserv, plus each program's eventual issuer
Each program's token, issuer, reserves and redemption promise
A client launches with terms in force and a named issuer
Fiserv markets a service using Paxos/Circle capabilities. It has not publicly established one FIUSD issuer with one set of rules, owners and terms.
A bank-branded token can hide a separate issuer partner.
Once each coin is eligible, Fiserv can add the payment method across existing merchant software.
Program terms, issuer charter or approval, contract address, reserve report and redemption commitment.
Treating the service provider as the issuer, or treating marketing as binding terms.
The StoneCastle deposit strategy does not prove how reserves are held now or who controls them.

items.title: SoFi's terms already allow it to move SOFID to a different issuer
kv: clause in current terms · not yet used
SoFi Bank, and an approved successor or subsidiary, under the contract
SOFID issuer rights and duties, and holders' claims
SoFi names or assigns a new issuer in response to the new stablecoin law
SoFi's current terms allow an added or substitute issuer and the transfer of issuer obligations.
Same ticker and app; a notice of the new issuer and revised terms.
No required change to hardware or acceptance.
Approval as a permitted payment stablecoin issuer (PPSI), a signed assignment or novation, updated terms and reserve disclosures.
A substitute issuer is announced, but holder liabilities are not actually transferred.
The clause shows SoFi is prepared; it does not prove the transfer has happened.

items.title: Tether once moved all of USD₮'s obligations to a new company (Jan 2025)
kv: Tether Limited and Tether International, S.A. de C.V.
All rights, duties and liabilities under the token contract, and user claims
Token terms effective 27 Jan 2025, and users' continued use
The old issuer assigned the token relationship to the new issuer, and users released the old entity.
Users accept new terms; they do not necessarily move wallets.
Usually invisible unless compliance or settlement policy changes.
Signed or in-force assignment language, effective date, assumption of liabilities and updated disclosures.
Calling a charter, an affiliate role or a marketing rename a novation (a full legal transfer of the contract).
Moving U.S. users from USD₮ to Anchorage-issued USA₮ would swap one product for another, not novate USD₮ in this way.

items.title: PayPal moved its wallet customers to PayPal Digital; the coin's issuer did not change
kv: completed change of the customer's contract party
PayPal, Inc. and PayPal Digital, Inc.
The customer's crypto account, custody and wallet contract
PayPal Digital became the customer's crypto-services counterparty. Paxos remained the PYUSD issuer and the company that owes redemption.
Same PayPal/Venmo apps, under a different contracting entity.
No change to the PYUSD issuer or the checkout page.
Current PayPal terms plus current Paxos stablecoin terms.
Mistaking the company on the customer contract for the issuer.
PayPal Digital's trust-company status does not make it the PYUSD issuer.
Newer record (Fed accounts and charters master)
Paxos: charter status 'opened'; latest step September 30, 2026: Listed on the OCC's active trust banks list (charter 25379).

uncertain: A stablecoin can keep the same ticker, wallet and payment terminal while its issuer, its reserve holder or its permission to be sold in the U.S. changes. Each card names who holds the legal power, what that party can change and what event lets it act.
A plan, a charter or a renamed service is not a change of issuer; only a signed assignment or novation with new terms is.
The deck's statutory dates, reserve holders, sellers and government orders are on the GENIUS Act timeline, stablecoin issuers and freeze pages.

catalog_context.title: OCC final stablecoin rules: issuer duties, permissions and operating evidence
catalog_context.answer: The OCC's final GENIUS rule takes effect January 18, 2027. Its requirements attach to specific issuers, claims and custody relationships; approval, backing, capital, reporting and completed redemption require separate evidence.

catalog_context.title: Which companies connect the new private money system
catalog_context.answer: No single coin or blockchain is taking over. Banks, crypto firms, card networks and market utilities each control a different step, and the most powerful firms may be the ones connecting those separate systems.
